title: Sampling-driven cachekey taxonomy and staged policy-apply for hit-rate-safe TTL tuning
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
We will build a sampling-driven pipeline to automatically infer a cachekey taxonomy (signature families) and evaluate TTL ladder candidates, plus a staged 'shadow-apply' and controlled rollout mechanism that enforces hit-rate preservation during production policy changes. The goal is to reduce per-token spend by improving effective cache hit-rate without regressions in tail latency or downstream correctness.

Background and motivation:
Current caching recommendations are hand-authored rules that often over- or under-shoot TTLs for diverse prefixes. Manual tuning is slow and risky: a bad TTL policy can evict hot prefixes or over-retain cold keys, increasing cost or staleness. We need an automated, feedback-driven method that 1) proposes cache-key groupings and TTL ladders from sampled traffic, 2) simulates economic impact and hit-rate delta, and 3) applies policies via a staged shadow-to-canary rollout with automated rollback guards.

Hypothesis:
1) A small sampled corpus (0.5-2% of requests) combined with lightweight feature extraction (token length, prompt fingerprint, route, customer tier, model) can produce stable 'signature families' that explain >80% of prefix hit-variance.
2) Hierarchical TTL ladders per signature family will yield at least 12% reduction in inference tokens served (model cost) with <1% degradation in observed P95 latency and <0.1% functional regressions on eval prompts.

Deliverables:
- Sampling extractor service (run-as-batch + streaming sampler) and storage schema for signature statistics.
- Offline hit-rate simulator that can replay sampled traffic against candidate key-group + TTL policies and produce cost/latency estimates.
- Cachekey taxonomy generator (clustering + rule synth) that outputs human-readable signature rules (e.g., route + first-token-hash-range + auth-tier).
- Staged policy applier: shadow mode -> limited canary (1% traffic) -> progressive ramp with automated rollback leash and manual approval step.
- Runbook and safety checks for rollback criteria and post-mortem templates.

Success metrics (target):
- Economic: >=12% mean token cost reduction for targeted routes in canary cohort.
- Quality: <=0.1% change in key quality signals (e.g., model output diff score) on evaluation prompts.
- Performance: <=1% relative increase in P95 request latency at steady state during rollout.
- Safety: Automated rollback triggers activate and revert policy within 5 minutes if hit-rate drop >5% or error rate increase >0.2%.

Plan & technical approach:
1) Data sampling (Sprint 1): instrument a 1% reservoir sampler in the gateway to capture canonicalized requests and minimal metadata. Respect PII: only store hashed prompt prefixes and route ids.
2) Feature extraction & taxonomy (Sprint 2): compute features (prefix length, distinctive token n-grams, route, customer_tier, model_variant) and apply an ensemble of clustering (HDBSCAN) + decision tree distillation to yield deterministic signature rules. Rule outputs must be interpretable for SRE/PM review.
3) Offline simulation (Sprint 2-3): build a replay harness that applies candidate TTL ladders to sampled traces and computes simulated hit-rate, token savings, and tail latency proxy (KV miss per second). Include shadow runs for edge cases.
4) Staged apply (Sprint 3-4): implement shadow-mode (no effect on live cache, but collects metrics), canary service that gates by tenant or route, and a ramp controller that monitors hit-rate delta and error signals.
5) Safety and rollback: implement rollback leash with hysteresis (must be stable drop >5% over 3 mins AND not explained by traffic spike) and a manual override via Console.

Data & infra requirements:
- Sampling storage (encrypted S3 or internal parquet store) with TTL of 90 days for experiments.
- Small simulation cluster (k8s job) to run replay within 30-60m for 1% sample of 24h traffic.
- Console dashboard to surface candidate policies, expected savings, and safety checks.

Risks & mitigations:
- Sampling bias: mitigate by stratified sampling across routes and tenant tiers.
- Privacy: only keep hashed prefix fingerprints and metadata; legal reviewing required.
- Model drift: track eval-set regressions per-policy and tie rollback thresholds to eval regressions as a secondary signal.
- Misclassification of signature: require human approval for newly synthesized rules that affect >5% traffic.

Rollout checklist (pre-canary):
- Simulation completed with >95% confidence intervals for hit-rate improvement.
- End-to-end integration tests for shadow-mode implemented and passing.
- Console page registering candidate policy and explicit assignee for manual approval.
- Security & privacy review completed (see attachments).

Cancellation criteria:
- If simulation indicates <6% cost improvement for target routes, deprioritize and iterate on taxonomy.
- If privacy review restricts storage of sufficient data, pivot to only metadata-driven heuristics.

Owners & stakeholders:
- Engineering owner: Mateo Alvarez (assignee)
- Data & modeling: Priya Singh (for hit-model validation)
- Product: Lucas Moretti (PM)
- SRE: Nora Patel (runbook + rollback automation)

Notes:
This ticket focuses on the synthesis and safe application mechanism; follow-on work will automate continuous re-tuning and integrate quantization/ batching suggestions into policy scoring.
